messages:
Mira: quick RFC follow-up: instead of central CP making every locality decision, can edge proxies own the quick path and get audited later?

Juan: Edge-first reduces RTTs but residency rules are strict for some tenants. If edge makes a wrong decision we need fast remediation.

Sam: Hybrid idea: edge picks candidate region and attaches a compact signed token from control-plane when available. CP verifies asynchronously and can issue eviction commands.

Olivia: Token schema suggestion (compact JWT): tenant, region, iat, exp, sig. Keep header <1KB. Edge caches token until exp.

Mira: How do we avoid serving stale writes from edge prefix caches if CP revokes a token mid-flight? Need a clear invalidation TTL or fast tombstone protocol.

Juan: Proposal: each edge cache entry annotated with attest_version and a monotonic evict_counter. On revoke CP increments evict_counter for tenant; edge compares and refuses cached prefixes with older counters.

Sam: For performance, attests are optional for non-sensitive tenants. Feature flag per-tenant: residency_mode = [strict, hybrid, delegated].

Olivia: Monitoring to add:
- locality.handshake_mismatch_rate
- locality.attest_verify_latency_p95
- locality.revoked_attests_count
- locality.cache_invalidation_delay_p99

Mira: Rollout plan: start hybrid in delegated mode for read-only tenants. Canary 0.5% traffic, then 5%. If mismatch_rate > 0.3% rollback.

deploy-bot: edge-proxy@canary deployed to 10% at 02:00 UTC.

Juan: Security note: tokens signed with CP KMS key; edge verifies signature. Rotation window: accept previous key for 1h after publishing new. Audit logs mandatory.

Sam: Action items: Juan -> implement evict_counter; Olivia -> dashboard panels; Mira -> canary checklist and RFC update; Sam -> edge token handling PoC.

Mira: I'll open the PRs and tag eng-sre. Thanks all.
